title: Yokai of Japan
subtitle: A Japanese Folklore Coloring Book of 50 Monsters for Adults and Teens, with Lore and Profile Cards
description:
Japan has the richest supernatural tradition in the world. These are its monsters illustrated from primary sources and yours to color.

Oni. Kitsune. Tengu. Kappa. Gashadokuro. For over a thousand years, Japan's artists and scholars have documented the creatures that inhabit its supernatural world. This illustrated bestiary brings fifty of them together in one volume each with a full-page illustration, complete lore drawn from original texts, and a profile card in English and Japanese.

Each creature gets four pages

Profile card - name in English and Japanese kanji, creature type, domain and three defining attributes. A collectible reference and a coloring page in one.
Lore page - researched from primary sources including the Kojiki, Toriyama Sekien's Gazu Hyakki Yagyo, the Heike Monogatari and Lafcadio Hearn's Kwaidan. Faces the illustration so the story stays visible while you color.
Full-page illustration - detailed monochrome line art at adult complexity. Dense, intricate, no shortcuts.
Blank backing page - so color bleeds nowhere. Pencils, fine liners, crayons and alcohol markers all work.
Fifty creatures including

title: Vættir of the Norse Eddas
subtitle: A Nordic Folklore Coloring Book of 50 Monsters for Adults and Teens, with Lore and Profile Cards
description:
The real creatures behind the myths: Draugr, Fenrir, Jörmungandr and the monsters of the Norse Eddas, illustrated and yours to color.

The world-serpent that encircles the ocean. The wolf whose jaws stretch from earth to sky. The undead warrior who rises from the burial mound with the strength of ten men. This illustrated bestiary gives you fifty creatures from Norse and Scandinavian mythology, each drawn from the original Eddas and sagas and ready to color.

Each creature includes four pages

A profile card with Old Norse name, Younger Futhark runic name, type, domain, nature and three sourced attributes
A full lore page researched from primary sources: the Prose Edda of Snorri Sturluson, the Poetic Edda, the Völsunga Saga and the Grettis Saga, always on the page facing the illustration
A full-page illustration in black-and-white line art, detailed and complex, made for adult coloring
A blank backing page behind every illustration to protect the next page; colored pencils and crayons recommended, alcohol markers may bleed
Fifty creatures across nine categories

title: Birds of India
subtitle: Colour Your Way Through India's Feathered World
description:
Vivid Wings. India's Feathered World. 50 Birds to Color.

India is home to over 1,300 species of birds, from snow-capped Himalayan peaks to sun-baked wetlands and tropical rainforests. This revised edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your coloring table.

From the fan-tailed Indian Peacock and the nine-colored Indian Pitta to the iridescent Himalayan Monal, the casque-crowned Great Hornbill, the soaring Brahminy Kite, the lily-pad-walking Pheasant-tailed Jacana, and the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard, every page features a different bird drawn in the style of a classic ornithological field guide.

Bold outlines. Accurate anatomy. Room to color. Each bird fills the full page with thick, crisp lines ideal for colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens. No cluttered backgrounds. Just one magnificent bird per page.

Every illustration is printed on its own page with a blank page behind it, so your colors stay on the right side. Colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens all work beautifully. Alcohol-based markers may bleed through to the blank backing page.

A fact on every page. Did you know the Bar-headed Goose flies over the Himalayas above 7,000 metres? That the Indian Pitta wears nine different colors on one tiny body? That fewer than 150 Great Indian Bustards remain in the wild today? You finish each page knowing the bird, not just coloring it.

Inside this book

50 full-page bird illustrations, one species per page
Common name, scientific name, and a fun fact on every illustration page
Full index of all 50 birds with page numbers
Species drawn to accurate proportions, not cartoon, not clipart

Part of the Birds of the World series. Suitable for children and adults who love birds and nature.

title: Birds of Brazil
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
50 Birds. One Coloring Book. Brazil's Feathered World.

Brazil is home to more bird species than any other country on Earth, over 1,900 in all. This expanded second edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your coloring table, from the iconic to the extraordinary.

From the cobalt-blue Hyacinth Macaw and the absurdly large-billed Toco Toucan to the seven-colored Paradise Tanager, the disc-crested Guianan Cock-of-the-rock, the ghostly White Hawk, and the wire-tailed Wire-tailed Manakin whose tail filaments brush a female's chin in courtship, every page features a different bird drawn in the style of a classic ornithological field guide.

Bold outlines. Accurate anatomy. Room to color. Each bird fills a full page with thick, crisp lines ideal for colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens. No cluttered backgrounds. Just one magnificent bird per page.

Each illustration is printed on one side of the page only, with a blank reverse, so you can color freely without worrying about bleed-through. Colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens are recommended. Alcohol-based markers may still bleed through depending on pressure applied.

A fact on every page. Did you know the Hyacinth Macaw can crack open a Brazil nut using only its beak? That the Sungrebe carries its chicks in feather pouches under its wings, even in flight? That the Amazonian Royal Flycatcher normally looks like a plain brown bird, but when alarmed raises a spectacular fan crest of brilliant orange-red feathers tipped with blue? Children and adults finish each page knowing the bird, not just coloring it.

Inside this book

50 full-page bird illustrations, one species per page, each on a single side
Common name and scientific name on every illustration page
Species drawn to accurate proportions, ornithological engraving style
An illustrated index listing all 50 birds with page numbers
Curated to showcase Brazil's remarkable diversity, from the Amazon to the cerrado to the Atlantic Forest

Part of the Birds of the World series. Volume 2. A coloring book for kids with 50 illustrations, scientific names and fun facts, suitable for children and adults who love birds and nature.

title: Birds of Costa Rica
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts

Costa Rica is home to more than 900 bird species packed into a country smaller than West Virginia, making it one of the richest birdwatching destinations on Earth. This expanded 2nd edition brings 50 of the most spectacular to your child's coloring table.

From the legendary Resplendent Quetzal, with tail streamers twice as long as its body, and the rainbow-billed Keel-billed Toucan to the thundering Three-wattled Bellbird, the walking-on-water Northern Jacana, and the Sunbittern whose open wings reveal two enormous false eyes, every page features a different bird drawn in the style of a classic ornithological field guide.

Bold outlines. Accurate anatomy. Room to color. Each bird fills the full page with thick, crisp lines ideal for colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens. No cluttered backgrounds. Just one magnificent bird per page.

Each illustration has its own dedicated page with a blank reverse side, so colors never bleed through. Use any coloring medium, including markers.

A fact on every page. Did you know the Harpy Eagle has talons as long as a grizzly bear's claws? That the Jabiru is the tallest flying bird in the Americas? That the male Long-tailed Manakin grows two wire-thin tail feathers purely to impress a mate? Children finish each page knowing the bird, not just coloring it.

Inside this book

50 full-page bird illustrations, one species per page
Common name and scientific name on every page
Species drawn to accurate proportions, not cartoon, not clipart
Curated to showcase Costa Rica's remarkable diversity of birdlife
Includes Costa Rica's national bird, the Clay-colored Thrush (Yigüirro)

Vol. 3 of the Birds of the World series. Ideal for children aged 6-9. Pick up your crayons. Costa Rica is waiting!

title: Birds of Madagascar
subtitle: Coloring Book for Kids with 50 Illustrations, Scientific Names and Fun Facts
description:
An Island Like No Other. 50 Birds Found Almost Nowhere Else on Earth.

Madagascar split from mainland Africa 160 million years ago and evolved in isolation. Over 100 of its bird species exist nowhere else on the planet. This book brings 50 of the most extraordinary to your coloring table.

From the Helmet Vanga with its absurdly enormous hooked bill to the Madagascar Fish Eagle, one of the rarest eagles on Earth with fewer than 200 pairs remaining, to the Long-tailed Ground-roller that lives only in a sliver of southwestern spiny desert, these are birds that could only exist on Madagascar. Every page features a different species drawn in the style of a classic ornithological engraving: bold outlines, accurate anatomy, room to color.

Each bird fills the full page with thick, crisp lines ideal for colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens. No cluttered backgrounds. Just one magnificent bird per page.

Every illustration is printed on its own page with a blank page behind it, so your colors stay on the right side. Colored pencils, crayons, and gel pens all work beautifully. Alcohol-based markers may bleed through to the blank backing page.

A fact on every page. Did you know the Madagascar Harrier-hawk has double-jointed knees that bend backward so it can reach into holes and pull out hidden lizards? That the Madagascar Jacana walks on floating lily pads on enormous spreading toes, appearing to walk on water? That the Cuckoo-roller is the only member of its entire bird family in the world? You finish each page knowing the bird, not just coloring it.

Inside this book

50 full-page bird illustrations, one species per page
Common name, scientific name, and a fun fact on every illustration page
Full index of all 50 birds with page numbers
Species drawn to accurate proportions, not cartoon, not clipart

Part of the Birds of the World series. Suitable for children and adults who love birds and nature.
